problems: data/polities.csv (1637 rows) is behind the dossiers (3007 files) and lacks many slugs used here (east-india-company, british-raj-era states, Neo-Assyrian vassals and others); every child and parent slug has a dossier of type state or dynasty, and check_hierarchy reads the dossiers, so this does not matter for R3.

Dating convention: 'to' is the year before the break event (so Israel ends -723, Judah/Edom/Moab/Ammon -609), or the shorter-lived dossier's identity end. Company rows end 1857 (the Crown takes over in 1858) and Raj rows end 1946, the year before the 1947 vassal_end, or at the child dossier's end.

east-india-company is the drawn parent of british-empire (same_state 1757-1858). Five Company pairs (bikaner-state, kota-state, jaisalmer-state, gwalior-state, kingdom-of-tripura) were dropped because hierarchy.csv already holds them under british-empire; kingdom-of-nagpur's Company row starts 1815 so it does not overlap the existing maratha-empire row (1752-1814).

Mongol rows use the united-empire years, ending 1259 (Mongke's death) for the uluses, and 1255 for Rum, Georgia and the Kartids so they do not overlap ulus-of-hulegu from 1256. Tibet under the Qing stops at 1909 because the 1910-12 occupation is booked separately.

Mirror gaps found (dossier fixes, not hierarchy rows): mughal-empire.json has no vassal_start for the Katoch rajas of Kangra 1620-1783 (the kangra-state row at confidence 2 rests on kangra-state.json plus the Kangra State page); tang-dynasty.json has no mirror of turks.json's vassal events 666-677 and 685-690; jhalawar-state.json says british-empire should record the 1838 vassal_start.
